description: spec 09 section 4.2 — the predicate behind the row a console renders for one stream. `refused` when the most recent thing that happened was a refusal, whatever the quiet interval says; `quiet` when nothing has been accepted within `quiet-after-seconds`; `healthy` otherwise. Which row an implementation draws is its own business; the predicate is not.

vectors.name: silent-past-the-interval-is-quiet
vectors.description: an absent emitter is a finding, not a null result — but it is the weaker finding

vectors.name: at-the-interval-exactly-is-still-healthy
vectors.description: the comparison is strict, so the row does not flicker on the boundary second

vectors.name: refused-after-the-last-acceptance-is-refused
vectors.description: the DEF-2 row. The last acceptance is a minute old, so nothing about quiet has fired and would not for an hour; the kernel nonetheless knows *now* that it is refusing this emitter, and the surface that exists to answer the question must say so

vectors.name: refused-and-then-silent-is-still-refused
vectors.description: the refusal is not superseded by the passage of time: quiet is the absence of evidence and this stream has evidence

vectors.name: refused-then-accepted-is-healthy-again
vectors.description: recovery is observable in the same surface: an acceptance after the refusal ends the refused state, which is what makes the row a state and not a scar

vectors.name: refused-in-the-same-millisecond-as-the-last-acceptance-is-refused
vectors.description: the tie breaks toward the finding. Three-decimal timestamps and a coarse deployment clock make this reachable, and the reading that hides a refusal is the one this state exists to stop

vectors.name: never-accepted-and-never-refused-is-quiet
vectors.description: a stream the kernel has heard nothing from at all

vectors.name: never-accepted-but-refused-is-refused
vectors.description: the emitter's very first submission was refused, so there is no acceptance to compare against — and this is precisely the mandate-swap-at-connect case
